papers.title_en: Gated Slot Attention-2: Two-Sided Associative Memory Correction in Linear Attention
papers.authors: Ruijie Li, Shengnan Ding, Weimin Zhang, Derick Tang, Zhanpeng Zeng, Qinsong Zeng, Ming Chen, Jiaxi Hu, Yuxuan Liang
papers.evidence: 线性注意力中的双侧联想记忆校正
papers.tldr: 线性注意力虽高效，但其固定大小循环记忆难以有效管理。已有delta规则侧重值端精确修正，Gated Slot Attention等槽架构分两阶段建模键值记忆，二者实为互补。本文提出Gated Oja Rule及Gated Oja Rule-2实现键端修正，并与Gated Delta Rule-2结合，构建Gated Slot Attention-2（GSA2），通过共享潜在槽同时修正关联两侧。作者还给出硬件高效的chunkwise并行训练算法。实验表明GSA2在多个基准上持续优于强线性注意力基线，同时保持线性时间建模与常数记忆循环解码。
papers.abstract_en: Linear attention models have emerged as efficient alternatives to standard attention, but effectively managing their fixed-size recurrent memory remains challenging. To improve memory, recent work has explored two distinct directions: delta-rule variants for precise correction of values associated with keys, and slot-based architectures such as Gated Slot Attention for modeling key and value memories in two stages. We observe that these directions are complementary--the delta rule provides effective memory correction, while the two-stage structure provides a natural way to operate on both sides of an association. Building on this insight, we introduce a new Gated Oja Rule for key-side correction and extend it with decoupled erase and write control to obtain Gated Oja Rule-2. We then introduce Gated Slot Attention-2 (GSA2), which combines Gated Oja Rule-2 for key-side correction with Gated Delta Rule-2 for value-side correction through shared latent slots. We further derive a hardware-efficient chunkwise algorithm for parallel training. Experiments demonstrate that GSA2 consistently improves over strong linear-attention baselines across benchmarks while retaining linear-time sequence modeling and constant-memory recurrent decoding.

papers.title_en: Adapting Linear-Time Architectures for Tabular In-Context Learning
papers.authors: David Schnurr, Felix Sarnthein, Thomas Hofmann, Imanol Schlag
papers.evidence: 面向上下文学习的线性时间序列混合器
papers.tldr: 表格基础模型依赖上下文标注样本，但softmax注意力限制大规模数据应用。本文系统比较因果训练与线性序列混合器，发现DeltaNet这一因果模型优于非因果线性注意力，却在外推至预训练长度2-4倍时退化。作者用时间依赖衰减调度稳定循环状态，并借末状态读出恢复非因果性。最终在OpenML-CC18和TabArena上接近受控softmax注意力基线。
papers.abstract_en: Tabular foundation models achieve strong performance by conditioning on labelled examples in context, but softmax attention limits their use on large datasets. Existing linear-time alternatives, however, are mostly causal, and their potential for tabular in-context learning (ICL) remains underexplored. To address this, we (1) revisit causal training setups, (2) compare linear sequence mixers, and (3) investigate their ICL generalisation beyond the pretraining context length. First, we show that the best training setup for causal models resembles next-token prediction. Then, perhaps surprisingly, the most promising linear sequence mixer is causal: DeltaNet outperforms even non-causal linear attention. However, it degrades beyond $2$-$4\times$ the pretraining context length, and existing mitigation strategies such as bidirectionality defer the problem at best. A hidden-state oracle shows that this is not a capacity problem. Instead, our analysis points to an instability in the recurrent state, which drifts in deeper layers of causal models. Since DeltaNet's learned write rates overfit to the pretraining regime, we modulate them with a time-dependent decay schedule intervention to stabilise length generalisation. Finally, re-introducing non-causality by reading out from the final state allows us to closely match a controlled softmax attention baseline on OpenML-CC18 and TabArena.

papers.title_en: The Evolution of Attention in Large Language Models: Mechanisms, Trade-offs, and Emerging Trends
papers.authors: Zhentao Tan, Jingyi Shen, Yanbo Li, Yao Liu, Yue Wu, Jieping Ye
papers.evidence: 把注意力视为模型内部上下文记忆的综述
papers.tldr: 自注意力提供细粒度上下文访问，但稠密交互带来二次预填充成本，KV缓存随上下文增长。本文将其视为模型内部上下文记忆，提出记忆表示、更新、访问、读出与整合五维视角，并基于14个模型谱系和11个开源权重端点的59条发布记录梳理机制与架构采用。研究指出显式记忆与循环状态功能日益重叠，异构架构跨层协调记忆，深度成为记忆构建维度，并提出有状态多维记忆路由假设。
papers.abstract_en: Self-attention gives LLMs fine-grained, query-dependent access to context, but dense token interactions incur quadratic prefill cost and a key--value cache growing with context length. Research thus spans explicit-memory compression, sparse access, recurrent state construction, structured state dynamics, and heterogeneous mechanism composition. This survey analyzes these developments as model-internal contextual memory. We introduce a five-dimensional lens---Memory Representation, Memory Update, Access, Readout, and Integration---describing what is represented, how it changes, what is query-eligible, how it is read, and how readouts form outputs. This lens compares overlapping research lines without imposing one computational model.   We reconstruct mechanism-level developments and architectural adoption using 59 release-level records from 14 major model lineages and 11 high-performing open-weight endpoints. First, explicit-memory and recurrent-state methods retain distinct interfaces but increasingly control overlapping memory functions. Second, heterogeneous architectures increasingly coordinate across network depth: layer-wise composition distributes complementary memory processing across representational stages, while cross-layer reuse carries selected memory and routing artifacts forward. Depth thus becomes a dimension along which contextual memory is constructed and managed. Third, these developments motivate a stateful multidimensional memory-routing hypothesis: persistent memory is organized across temporal scope, network depth, substrate type, and representation granularity, while coordinated Sparse Write and Sparse Read determine what is maintained and what contributes to each query. Overall, efficient sequence architecture design increasingly concerns the organization, lifecycle, and selective use of contextual memory rather than an isolated Attention operator.

papers.title_en: Role-aware Heuristic Episodic Attention for Conversational LLMs
papers.authors: Wanyang Hong, Zhaoning Zhang, Yi Chen, Libo Zhang, Baihui Liu, Linbo Qiao, Zhiliang Tian, Dongsheng Li
papers.evidence: 面向对话大模型的情景注意力记忆管理
papers.tldr: 多轮对话中，LLM 常因上下文累积而遗忘持久指令与关键信息，出现注意力污染、稀释和漂移。REA 将指令与情景交互分开管理：指令存入专用前缀，情景记忆保留用户输入并压缩模型回复，启发式检索逐轮选择原文、压缩表示或省略。在 Long-MT-Bench+ 上，REA 将评分从 6.32 提升至 7.36（16.5% 相对增益），延迟降低 2.91 倍。在 1.7B-7B 三个骨干及中英文角色扮演任务上也有总体提升，表明角色感知上下文管理能维持对话连续性与指令遵循。
papers.abstract_en: Large language models often lose track of persistent instructions and relevant information as multi-turn conversations grow. We study this cumulative contextual decay through three related failure modes: attention pollution, dilution, and drift. We propose REA (Role-aware Heuristic Episodic Attention), a context-management framework that assigns different persistence and representation policies to instructions and episodic interactions. Instructional Memory retains identified global constraints in a dedicated prefix. Episodic Memory preserves user inputs and compresses model replies, while heuristic retrieval selects raw text, compressed representations, or omission for each historical turn. On Long-MT-Bench+, REA improves the judge score from 6.32 to 7.36 on a 10-point scale, a 16.5% relative gain over the Vanilla baseline, and reduces average latency by 2.91$\times$. Additional evaluations show aggregate gains on three backbones spanning 1.7B-7B parameters and on Chinese and English role-playing tasks. These results support role-aware context management as a practical approach to maintaining conversational continuity and instruction adherence.

papers.title_en: VASC: Value-Aware Sparse Attention with Cross-Layer Memory for Efficient 3D Reconstruction
papers.authors: Junyi Wu, Fanqing Kong, Leyang Chen, Shaoqiu Zhang, Yulun Zhang
papers.evidence: 带跨层记忆的稀疏注意力提升效率
papers.tldr: VGGT等前馈3D模型可单次完成相机估计与稠密重建，但全局注意力二次开销使长序列推理昂贵；现有稀疏方法易保留高注意力却值冗余的区域。VASC提出免训练稀疏注意力，融合池化query-key相关性与邻域值对比选块，并用跨层记忆追踪未满足需求，在固定预算下重分配计算。在7Scenes与NeuralRGB-D上结合VGGT和π^3，姿态与重建优于FasterVGGT，推理较稠密VGGT最高加速2.29倍，为高效3D重建提供免训练方案。
papers.abstract_en: Feed-forward 3D vision models such as VGGT have achieved remarkable progress, unifying camera estimation and dense scene reconstruction in a single pass. However, their quadratic global attention makes long image sequences expensive, while existing sparse methods may favor highly attended yet value-redundant regions. To address these limitations, we introduce VASC, a training-free sparse attention method combining value-aware block selection and execution-aware cross-layer memory. Our value-aware block selection integrates pooled query--key relevance with neighboring value contrast, reducing redundancy while preserving query-relevant and distinctive content. Cross-layer memory tracks unserved demand across layers and updates this state according to actual execution, enabling previously underserved blocks to compete under a fixed computation budget. Experiments on 7Scenes and NeuralRGB-D with VGGT and $π^3$ demonstrate improved pose estimation and reconstruction quality compared with FasterVGGT, together with up to $2.29\times$ faster inference than dense VGGT. Code is available at https://github.com/kosakayamahoo-design/VASC.

papers.title_en: APDMem: Agent-Controlled Progressive Disclosure for Query-Adaptive Long-Term Memory
papers.authors: Chin-Lun Fu, Anagha Kulkarni, Hong Ni, Behrouz Madahian
papers.evidence: 分层长期记忆与自适应检索控制器
papers.tldr: 个性化LLM助手需从长对话中检索稀疏证据，但查询复杂度各异。APDMem提出分层长期记忆架构，将历史组织为主题摘要、个性化关键事实、轮次级证据笔记与原始消息四层。推理时由控制器渐进式披露：先读高层摘要，按需深入细粒度证据，实现成本与保真度的自适应权衡。笔记合成器进一步整合事实、排序事件并标记矛盾。在LongMemEval上，仅访问8%对话即取得强长上下文记忆推理性能。
papers.abstract_en: Personalized LLM assistants must recover sparse evidence from long conversation histories across queries of varying complexity. We introduce APDMem (Agent-controlled Progressive Disclosure Memory), a hierarchical long-term memory architecture that applies progressive disclosure to memory retrieval. Rather than relying on a flat memory store or fixed retrieval granularity, APDMem represents conversation history as four progressively detailed layers: thematic summaries, personalized key facts, turn-level evidence notes, and raw messages. At inference time, a controller applies progressive disclosure to the memory hierarchy: it first reads high-level summaries and drills into finer evidence only when needed. This creates an adaptive cost-fidelity trade-off: simple queries can terminate early, while complex temporal, multi-hop, or exact-evidence queries trigger deeper inspection. A note synthesizer converts retrieved evidence into a query-focused structure that consolidates facts, orders events, and flags contradictions before final answer generation. Experiments on LongMemEval show that APDMem achieves strong performance for long-context memory reasoning while accessing only 8% of the total conversations.
